domain_restrictions: b, m, and d are integers and each is at least 0
t ranges over positive integers only
q is a formal indeterminate, not a numerical parameter
the product defining F_{b,m,d}(q) is finite and uses the convention that the empty product equals 1 when m equals 0
Phi_t(q) is the standard t-th cyclotomic polynomial
the cyclotomic factorization is understood for the rational function in q, so exponents may be interpreted as multiplicities in a factorization of a rational function
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For every nonnegative integer triple b, m, d, the t-th cyclotomic polynomial appears in the factorization of F_{b,m,d}(q) with exponent equal to floor((b+d+m)/t) minus floor((b+d)/t) minus floor((b+m)/t) plus floor(b/t), for every positive integer t. Moreover, F_{b,m,d}(q) is a polynomial in q exactly when, for every positive integer t, floor((b+m)/t) minus floor(b/t) is less than or equal to floor((b+d+m)/t) minus floor((b+d)/t); in that case the polynomial has integer coefficients.
quantifier_order: for all integers b, m, d with b, m, d nonnegative
define F_{b,m,d}(q) using the finite product, with the empty product equal to 1 when m equals 0
for each positive integer t, define Phi_t(q) as the t-th cyclotomic polynomial
for each positive integer t, the exponent of Phi_t(q) in the cyclotomic factorization of F_{b,m,d}(q) is the stated floor-expression
for each fixed b, m, d, F_{b,m,d}(q) is a polynomial in q if and only if the stated inequality holds for every positive integer t
in the polynomial case, F_{b,m,d}(q) lies in Z[q]

statement_nl: For integers b, m, and d with b >= 0, m >= 0, and d >= 0, define F_{b,m,d}(q) := product_{i=1}^m (1 - q^(b+d+i)) / (1 - q^(b+i)), with the empty product equal to 1 when m = 0. For each positive integer t, let Phi_t(q) denote the t-th cyclotomic polynomial. Then the exponent of Phi_t(q) in the cyclotomic factorization of the rational function F_{b,m,d}(q) is (floor((b+d+m)/t) - floor((b+d)/t)) - (floor((b+m)/t) - floor(b/t)). Consequently, F_{b,m,d}(q) is a polynomial in q if and only if floor((b+m)/t) - floor(b/t) <= floor((b+d+m)/t) - floor((b+d)/t) for every positive integer t; in that case F_{b,m,d}(q) actually lies in Z[q].
